page: Microsoft Azure E64ds_v7 is an Edsv7-family virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. This server includes 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a 3780 GB local NVMe SSD, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 89771.17 placing it in the top tier. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), contribute to strong cryptographic and vector execution. In memory-bound operations, the system achieves a read-only cached small-block bandwidth of 5421.5 GB/sec and a large-block uncached read bandwidth of 332.26 GB/sec. For database workloads, it demonstrates strong performance with 117.01 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a PassMark database score of 33062.35. Static web serving throughput is also top-tier at 110.35 GB/sec.

While prompt processing for large language models is highly efficient, reaching top-tier speeds of 4079.59 tokens/sec for small models and 39.93 tokens/sec for large models, text generation speeds remain average, such as 4.31 tokens/sec for a 70B model, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. Given the high memory density, fast local NVMe storage, and strong multi-core capabilities, this instance is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale Redis deployments, enterprise web serving, and data-heavy analytical workloads.
